newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end higher on institutional buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end higher on institutional buying.

text.p: A late buying spree by domestic financial institutions coupled with short-covering by speculators lifted share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange to a higher close on Tuesday, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 7.18 points higher at 712.53.
Brokers said investors were waiting for the government to follow through on a promise to announce steps to bolster capital markets before staking out fresh positions.
"The market's sentiment remained firm mainly on expectations of a package of incentives from the government to revive capital market," said Anil Saigal of brokers Anil Saigal.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said last week that the government planned by mid-January to announce moves to boost industrial production and revive capital markets.
Another trader said the rise in share prices was aided by the return of foreign financial institutions (FIIs) as buyers.
Reliance Industries firmed 3.75 rupees to 219.05 on heavy buying by domestic mutual funds coupled with short-covering by speculators, brokers said.
State Bank of India gained 6.20 rupees to 247.20 on institutional buying, they said.
TISCO surged 8.90 rupees to 189.25 on foreign buying.
Larsen and Toubro quoted 2.70 rupees higher at 232.50 on speculative buying.
